chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us; he said: Narrated to me a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him),

regarding the saying of the Exalted: 'So if they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their own desires. And who is more astray than he who follows his desire without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.'
He said: It means one who made his own opinion his religion, without an Imam from the Imams of Guidance.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to follow one's desires in religion according to Shia exegesis?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Hadi (or Imam al-Askari, depending on the specific chain interpretation) interprets the phrase 'following their desires' in Surah Muhammad as a critique of those who adopt personal opinion (*ra'y*) as their sole religious authority, lacking a divinely appointed Imam. This exegesis underscores the Shia doctrine that true guidance requires adherence to the *A'immat al-Huda* (Imams of Guidance), positioning the Imamate as the essential counterpart to the Quran for preventing religious deviation. It highlights the transition from individual interpretation to institutionalized divine authority in Shia jurisprudence.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (7) Muhammad bin Ya’qoob narrated from some of his companions from Ahmad bin Muhammad from ibn Abu Nasr that Imam Abul Hasan (ar-Redha) had said when talking about the Qur’anic verse, “
…And who is more erring than he who follows his low desires without any guidance from Allah?” “
It means one, who depends upon his own opinion in the affairs of religion without following an imam of the imams of guidance.”
